title: ISO 42001 Annex A Control A.9 – Use of AI Systems
description: Annex A Control A.9 focuses on the responsible use of AI systems, ensuring organisations follow policies that guide ethical, transparent, and accountable AI system utilisation.

subtitle: Purpose & Key Components
content: Control A.9 mandates clear processes and objectives for AI use, detailed documentation, risk management strategies, and continuous monitoring to foster trust, reliability, and ethical innovation.

subsections.heading: Purpose and Contribution to Responsible AI Use
subsections.content: The primary purpose of Annex A Control A.9 is to guide organisations in the ethical, transparent, and accountable use of AI systems. By setting a global standard, it aims to foster trust and reliability in AI technologies across various sectors. This control contributes to responsible AI use by mandating detailed documentation, risk management strategies, and continuous monitoring of AI systems’ performance.

subsections.heading: Key Components for Compliance Officers
list: Processes for Responsible Use: Defining and documenting how AI systems should be responsibly used within the organisation.
Objectives for Responsible Use: Identifying and documenting the goals guiding the ethical use of AI, such as fairness, accountability, and transparency.
Intended Use Compliance: Ensuring AI systems are used as intended, with necessary documentation and monitoring in place.

title: Processes for Responsible Use of AI Systems

subsections.heading: Defining and Documenting Processes
subsections.content: Establish and record specific workflows for AI use—including approvals, cost and sourcing requirements, and legal/regulatory compliance—making them accessible to all stakeholders.

subsections.heading: Implementation and Oversight
subsections.content: Integrate documented processes into existing management systems, align with organisational goals, and empower compliance officers to review, update, and enforce them regularly.

title: Objectives for Responsible Use of AI Systems

subsections.heading: Identifying and Documenting Objectives
subsections.content: Define goals such as fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability, reliability, safety, privacy, and accessibility by engaging stakeholders across departments.

subsections.heading: Challenges in Aligning AI Use with Objectives
subsections.content: Balance innovation with ethical constraints, adapt to evolving regulations, and build consensus among diverse stakeholders to overcome alignment hurdles.

subsections.heading: Benefits of Establishing Clear Objectives
subsections.content: Provides a structured decision-making framework, ensures compliance with values and regulations, mitigates risks, and supports human oversight and performance monitoring.

title: Intended Use of the AI System

subsections.heading: Ensuring Compliance with Intended Use
subsections.content: Use AI systems only for their documented purposes, guided by deployment instructions and performance expectations to prevent misuse.

subsections.heading: Required Documentation
subsections.content: Maintain comprehensive records of intended uses, resource needs, and human-oversight criteria to verify lawful and ethical operation.

subsections.heading: Monitoring and Enforcement Mechanisms
subsections.content: Employ automated tools and human review to detect deviations, then trigger predefined protocols for correction and stakeholder notification.

subsections.heading: Addressing Deviations from Intended Use
subsections.content: Log and investigate non-compliance events, enabling transparent reporting and swift remediation to maintain ethical and operational parameters.

subsections.heading: Unique Risks Associated with AI Systems
subsections.content: AI introduces biases, fairness concerns, privacy and security risks, and operational reliability challenges distinct from traditional IT systems.

subsections.heading: Dynamic Risk Identification and Analysis
subsections.content: Continuously monitor AI throughout its lifecycle using automated assessment tools to detect emerging threats in real-time.

subsections.heading: Tailored Strategies for AI-Specific Risks
subsections.content: Implement bias-mitigation guidelines, data-protection measures, and robust monitoring tailored to each AI application and context.

subsections.heading: Effective Risk Management and Responsible AI Use
subsections.content: Identify, analyze, and address AI risks to operate ethically and reliably, building stakeholder trust and aligning with ISO 42001 standards.

subsections.heading: Strategic Approaches for AI Objectives Setting
subsections.content: Align AI goals with organisational strategy using SMART criteria and involve cross-department stakeholders for a holistic roadmap.

subsections.heading: Ensuring Adaptability in AI Initiatives
subsections.content: Foster continuous learning and flexibility to pivot strategies as technologies evolve and regulatory landscapes change.

subsections.heading: Considerations for Resource Allocation
subsections.content: Assess tools, technologies, talent, and ongoing maintenance costs to prioritize investments with the greatest impact on AI objectives.

subsections.heading: Impact of Operational Planning on the AI Lifecycle
subsections.content: Plan resources proactively to avoid shortages, align objectives, and ensure scalability, sustaining AI systems’ effectiveness over time.
